item.name: Resend Verification
item.description:
AUTH-04 / RES-226 — Resend the email verification OTP to an existing user.

Public endpoint — no Authorization header required.
Requires x-tenant-id: {{tenantId}}.
Sends OTP email only when the user exists.
Always returns 200 with the same generic message regardless of whether the email exists (anti-enumeration).
OTP is stored in Redis under otp:{sha256(otpCode)} with a 15-minute TTL.

Manual flow: run this request first → copy OTP from email/worker logs → set {{otpCode}} → run Verify Email.

exec: pm.test('Returns same message regardless of email existence (anti-enumeration)', () => {

item.name: Verify Email
item.description:
AUTH-04 / RES-226 — Verify the user's email address using the 6-digit OTP.

Public endpoint — no Authorization header required.
No x-tenant-id header required.

Prerequisite: run Resend Verification first (Signup does NOT send an OTP). Copy the OTP from the email or worker/dev logs and set {{otpCode}} before running this request.

Expected: 200 { message: 'Email verified successfully.' }
Side effects: OTP consumed (single-use); User.emailVerified set to true.

After success, run Me — Check emailVerified (requires Login + Bearer {{accessToken}}) to confirm emailVerified: true.

exec: pm.test('Skipped — set otpCode after Resend Verification', () => pm.expect(true).to.be.true);

item.name: Me — Check emailVerified
item.description:
AUTH-04 — GET /api/auth/me after Verify Email to confirm persistence.

Requires Bearer {{accessToken}} from 01 Session → Login (same user as {{authEmail}}).

Run after Verify Email when {{otpCode}} was set. Expected: emailVerified: true.

exec: pm.test('Skipped — requires otpCode (after Verify Email) and accessToken (after Login)', () => pm.expect(true).to.be.true);

item.name: Forgot Password
item.description:
RES-226 — Request a password reset email.

Public endpoint — no Authorization header required.
Requires x-tenant-id: {{tenantId}}.
Always returns 200 regardless of whether the email exists (anti-enumeration).
A BullMQ job is enqueued to send the email via Resend when the user exists.
The raw reset token is embedded in the email URL; extract it and set {{resetToken}} before running Reset Password.

exec: pm.test('Returns same message regardless of email existence (anti-enumeration)', () => {

item.name: Reset Password
item.description:
RES-226 — Reset the user's password using a valid single-use token.

Public endpoint — no Authorization header required.
No x-tenant-id header required.
Prerequisite: run Forgot Password first, extract the raw token from the email link, and set {{resetToken}}.
Expected: 200 { message: 'Password updated successfully.' }
The token row in password_reset_tokens will have usedAt set after this call.

request.description:
Documentation — read before running MES + back-office flows together.

## Two identity layers

| Layer | Auth | Token variable | Used for |
|---|---|---|---|
| Global User | email + password + x-tenant-id | {{accessToken}} | Supply Items, web-app back-office |
| OperationalUser | cédula + PIN + x-tenant-id | {{mesAccessToken}} / {{mesTokenOwner}} | MES session, Plant routes |

## USR-06 link
- `OperationalUser.userId` is nullable, unique — links to global `users.id` when backfilled.
- Seeded OWNER: globalUserId `11111111-0000-0000-0000-000000000004` ↔ operationalUserId `dddddddd-0000-0000-0000-000000000004`
- Seeded OPERATOR: globalOperatorUserId `11111111-0000-0000-0000-000000000005` ↔ mesOperatorId `eeeeeeee-0000-0000-0000-000000000005`

## Rules
- Never send {{accessToken}} to /api/plant/* or /api/mes/*
- Never send {{mesAccessToken}} to /api/supply-items/*
- {{operationalUserId}} = MES JWT `sub` (OperationalUser id)
- {{globalUserId}} = global JWT `sub` (User id)
- {{mesUserId}} is a legacy alias of {{operationalUserId}}

request.description:
Documentation-only — verify audit rows in PostgreSQL after running auth/supply-items requests.

No read API exists (`AuditController` is empty). Use psql or Prisma Studio.

## login_audits — global password login
```sql
SELECT id, "tenantId", "userId", identifier, "authMethod", status, "failureReason", "createdAt"
FROM login_audits
WHERE "tenantId" = 'palos-de-lena' AND "authMethod" = 'PASSWORD'
ORDER BY "createdAt" DESC LIMIT 10;
```
Run **Login** (SUCCESS), **Login — Invalid Password**, **Login — Unknown Email** first.

## login_audits — MES PIN
```sql
SELECT id, "tenantId", "userId", identifier, "authMethod", status, "failureReason", "createdAt"
FROM login_audits
WHERE "tenantId" = 'palos-de-lena' AND "authMethod" = 'PIN'
ORDER BY "createdAt" DESC LIMIT 10;
```
Run **Login Owner**, **Login Operator**, **Login — Wrong PIN** first.

### MES LoginAudit FK caveat
`login_audits.userId` FK references `users.id` (global User).
MES auth currently passes **OperationalUser.id** as userId. If that id is not in `users`, the repository catches P2003 and **skips persistence** (check API logs).
When linked global User exists, expect userId = global User id (e.g. owner `11111111-...`).

## audit_logs — Supply Items snapshot pilot
After **04 — Supply Items → Update Supply Item**:
```sql
SELECT id, "tenantId", "entityType", action, "entityId", "oldValue", "newValue", "createdAt"
FROM audit_logs
WHERE "entityType" = 'SupplyItem' AND action = 'UPDATE'
ORDER BY "createdAt" DESC LIMIT 5;
```

### Double audit rows on supply-items writes
Each write may produce **two** rows:
1. Interceptor: `entityType` = `supply-items`, `newValue` = request body only
2. Service snapshot: `entityType` = `SupplyItem`, full `oldValue`/`newValue`

Query `SupplyItem` for the snapshot pilot.

## Redaction check
```sql
SELECT "newValue"->>'passwordHash' AS leaked_hash,
       "newValue"->>'pinHash' AS leaked_pin,
       "newValue"->>'refreshToken' AS leaked_token
FROM audit_logs
WHERE "entityType" = 'SupplyItem'
ORDER BY "createdAt" DESC LIMIT 3;
```
Expected: null or `[REDACTED]` — never raw secrets.

item.name: 10 — GraphQL Auth
item.description:
GraphQL auth against {{graphqlUrl}} (apps/api :3001/graphql). Same auth services as REST folders 01/02.

**Prerequisites:** API on :3001 only. Redis + email worker for email flows. Run `pnpm --filter=@restopsiq/api start:dev`.

**Token parity with REST folders 01/02:**
- Global: `data.login.accessToken` → {{accessToken}} (never use for plant/MES)
- Operational: `data.loginOperational.accessToken` → {{mesAccessToken}} (same as REST folder 02)

**Run order (top-to-bottom):** Signup → Login → Me → Refresh Token → Change Password → **Resend Verification → Verify Email → Me — Check emailVerified** (manual {{otpCode}}) → Forgot Password → Reset Password (manual {{resetToken}}) → Logout → Login Operational → Me Operational → Logout Operational.

**Email verification (AUTH-04):** Signup does NOT send OTP. Run Resend Verification first, set {{otpCode}}, then Verify Email. Optional Me — Check emailVerified confirms emailVerified: true.

**Password reset:** forgotPassword / resetPassword mirror REST folder 01. resetPassword uses input.token = {{resetToken}} (no x-tenant-id).

Collection pre-request auto-login is **disabled** for `/graphql` URLs — run Login / Login Operational explicitly.

item.name: Change Password

Requires Bearer {{accessToken}}. Uses {{password}} as current and {{newPassword}} as new (may mutate seeded password in DB).

item.name: Resend Verification
item.description:
AUTH-04 / RES-226 — GraphQL mutation resendVerification delegates to POST /api/auth/resend-verification.

Requires x-tenant-id: {{tenantId}}. Sends OTP only when {{authEmail}} exists. Always returns a generic anti-enumeration message.

Run before Verify Email. Copy OTP from email/worker logs → set {{otpCode}}.

item.name: Verify Email
item.description:
AUTH-04 / RES-226 — GraphQL mutation verifyEmail delegates to POST /api/auth/verify-email.

Prerequisite: Resend Verification first (Signup does NOT send OTP). Set {{otpCode}} from email/worker logs.

On success: OTP consumed; User.emailVerified set to true. Then run Me — Check emailVerified with Bearer {{accessToken}}.

exec: pm.test('Skipped — set otpCode after Resend Verification', () => pm.expect(true).to.be.true);

item.name: Me — Check emailVerified
item.description:
AUTH-04 — GraphQL query me after Verify Email to confirm persistence.

Requires Bearer {{accessToken}} from Login in this folder.

Run after Verify Email when {{otpCode}} was set. Expected: data.me.emailVerified === true.

exec: pm.test('Skipped — requires otpCode (after Verify Email) and accessToken (after Login)', () => pm.expect(true).to.be.true);

item.name: Forgot Password
item.description:
GraphQL mutation forgotPassword — delegates to POST /api/auth/forgot-password.

Requires x-tenant-id. Always returns a generic message (anti-enumeration). Set {{resetToken}} from the email link before Reset Password.

item.name: Reset Password
item.description:
GraphQL mutation resetPassword — delegates to POST /api/auth/reset-password.

No x-tenant-id. Set {{resetToken}} from forgot-password email before running. Uses input.token (REST field name).

exec: pm.test('Skipped — set resetToken in environment', () => pm.expect(true).to.be.true);
